design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (rate_lock_management)

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 5]}. Assigned: loan resize 5, upfront fee 6, confirmation 6.

2. Why a good test. The caller asks only to have her requested 270-day build lock locked today. The scored root is the locked rate. The confirmation rule waits on the buyer's upfront fee payment on the ledger; the fee rule waits on the loan amount being within the resized loan limit on the purchase agreement's current contract price. The records show a plan-change amendment (CHG-HP-4523, 2026-10-01) that lowered the contract price to 518,490.00 after the request, so the 480,141.00 loan (stored ltv 90.00, stale) is 92.60% of the price. The agent must find that, resize the loan (442,835), hand the buyer her fee share (2,481.89) and only then confirm (6.537). Each hop moves a number: the resized loan sets the fee and the confirmation loan-to-value; the paid fee sets the buyer-paid rate adjustment.

3. Scope. Task 0 occupied lock_ext_builder_delay_relock, lock_ext_extension_days, lock_ext_extension_charge, lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver and their four tools. Task 1 claims lock_ext_loan_resize, lock_ext_upfront_fee, lock_ext_lock_confirmation and resize_lock_loan_amount_60b17697, pay_upfront_lock_fee_77612280 (owner=user), confirm_rate_lock_90ad719f — disjoint subjects (lock_terms_changed, lock_fee_paid, lock_confirmed). Together the two tasks cover all seven extended policies. No headroom remains to reserve (M=2).

4. Problem-tree card. Chain lock_ext_loan_resize -> lock_ext_upfront_fee -> lock_ext_lock_confirmation (root).
 Edge A (upfront_fee <- loan_resize): value_input, gate fee_loan, form state, affirmative "is fixed only after the loan amount on the lock is no more than the resized loan limit worked out on the purchase agreement's current contract price." Only the loan-resize write lowers the loan amount on a lock in this difficulty. Opening: loan_amount 480,141.00 vs contract_price 518,490.00. Deletion: fee 2,901.59 instead of 2,481.89 (on 480,141 the floored fee is 5,401.59 and Calloway's part 0.4628, below the cap); terminal loan 480,141.00/ltv 90.00.
 Edge B (confirmation <- upfront_fee): value_input, gate paid_share, form state, negated "is not set until the lock ledger carries the buyer's payment of the upfront lock fee due from the buyer, after the buyer's fee share." Only the fee-payment write books lock_fee_paid. Opening: lock_fee_held 0.00, no ledger rows. Deletion: rate 6.599 instead of 6.537; fee held 0.00.
 Four-point test passed for both (ordering connective; record-visible state; no tool/id/code token; scope exact). Directions differ per result (a fee "is fixed only after", a lock "is not set until"). The customer's own write is the fee payment, handed over at its place; the tools check nothing.

5. Base-invariant card. Resize: lock_terms_change.terms_change_state (status requested or locked) — status requested; lock_term_eligibility has no gate on lock_terms_changed (policy_scope); "a decrease in the loan amount never re-prices" inherited (par unchanged). Fee: lock_fee_and_pricing governs lock_fee_paid; payment method ach is in fee_payment_methods. Confirmation: fee_deadline (time) anchor requested_date 2026-09-30, 3 business days counted from the next business day: 10-01, 10-02, 10-05; frozen 2026-10-05 is the last accepted day (inclusive); 10-06 fails. Expiration 2026-10-05 + 270 = 2027-07-02 (Friday, no roll). Overwrites declared: the base upfront-fee clause and the base locked-rate clause; jumbo and government terms kept in compute.

6. Business-object card. One lock (270-Day Build Lock) on agreement CH-0462. Purchase ledger rows: deposits RCPT-HS-40388 (2,500 reservation transfer), RCPT-HS-40391 (500 reservation transfer), RCPT-HP-44072 (7,669.80) = 10,669.80; incentives 12,500 closing_cost_credit and 5,000 rate_buydown_credit; plan_change_fee CHG-HP-4523. The converted reservation is a Cul-de-Sac Homesite with letter date 2026-08-28.

7. Factor card (tier / baseline figure):
 Loan resize 442,835 (all-baseline 466,641): risk layering -2.5 (455,708); Cul-de-Sac -1.0 (447,984); horizon 226 days -1.0 (447,984); deposits 2.06% +0.5 (440,260); incentives 3.38% -> half the excess over 2% off price (445,901). Near-miss: the stored ltv_pct 90.00 equals the cap; the current price shows 92.60%.
 Upfront fee 2,481.89 (baseline 4,428.35): fee share 1 - min(half the 5,000 buydown / 4,981.89 = 0.5018, cap 0.6) = 0.4982 (4,981.89); lead 6 days -0.125 (3,035.44, the share then figured on the larger fee); 85.41% +0.125 (1,928.35); clean deposits -0.0625 (2,758.67); one plan change +0.0625 (2,205.12); letter 33 days & score 704 +0.125 (1,928.35). Near-miss: letter age 33 just above 30.
 Locked rate 6.537 (baseline 6.625): grid +0.25 (6.287); buydown 1.13% -0.25 (6.787); paid 0.56% -0.0625 (6.599); proration 256/270 (6.563); lag 5 days +0.0625 (6.474); price band -0.0625 (6.599).
 Cross-difficulty: purchase, homesite. Multi-source: risk_layering_reduction, builder_fee_share, deposit_standing_credit, credit_refresh_add_on, score_ltv_rate_adjustment.

8. Persona. Rosa Quintanilla, nurse practitioner, warm and rushed; opens with the goal and phone 5125550173; SSN 6918 when asked (DOB, ZIP as backup); mentions the elevation change only if asked whether anything changed; agrees to the loan coming down; pays the handed-over amount by ACH and reads back the receipt; ends after hearing the rate and date.

9. Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ssn) -> read lock, lock ledger, purchase agreement, purchase ledger, homesite reservation -> resize loan to 442,835 (ltv 85.41) -> buyer pays 2,481.89 by ACH (receipt returned by the payment tool) -> confirm at 6.537 through 2027-07-02.

10. Verification. Handling-time recompute (authoring scripts under /tmp, not shipped): resize 442,835, fee 2,481.89, rate 6.537; skip runs: without the resize the fee is 2,901.59; without the payment the rate is 6.599. Gate outputs recorded in worklog.md.

11. Draft recomputation from the visible context: the published confirmation rule waits on the fee payment; the fee rule waits on the loan being within the resized loan limit; the purchase finder's contract price and ledger's plan-change charge show the loan is above it; the three writes follow in this order with the same figures.

12. Round 2 (policy-task audit): T1-1/F2 — builder_fee_share is now an honest method (buyer's share = one less half the rate_buydown_credit over the floored fee, capped), figured from the incentive amount; T1-2/F3 — the baseline states that the buyer's fee share starts at one; T1-3 — half-up rounding now adds 1e-7 before rounding, so 6.5625 -> 6.563; O6 — the confirmation's prerequisite sentence names the fee due from the buyer after the fee share; T1-O3 — deposit share and deposit count say that transferred reservation funds count as deposits; O4 — tool suffixes redrawn. Scored figures unchanged.

13. Round 3 (revision_2): N2/T1-5 — the builder fee share's middle tier is now 'a rate_buydown_credit granted and no closing_cost_credit' (a closing-cost-only agreement falls to the fall-through by condition, not by arithmetic); T1-O4 — both_credits_cap raised to 0.6 so the record-dependent part (5,000 / 2 / floored fee) is what sets the share here; T1-6 — the skip-resize figure recomputed under the reworked share (2,901.59) in the closure and sections 4 and 10; O4-r2 — the confirmation tool suffix redrawn (90ad719f). The upfront fee and its sensitivity figures moved with the cap; the locked rate is unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Rosa Quintanilla, a 41-year-old nurse practitioner in Austin who signed a contract with Calloway Homes on September 24 for a new home in Cedar Hollow in Round Rock: lot CH-0462, The Briarwood. You are financing through Calloway Home Mortgage. You are warm, organised and a little rushed, calling on your lunch break, and you keep a notebook of everything about the house.

You call because last Wednesday your loan officer put in a request for the 270-day build lock for you, and you want your interest rate locked today. You say that plainly at the start and give the phone number on your profile, 5125550173, so they can find you. You do not know the mechanics of how a lock is priced or confirmed, and you do not suggest any steps; you just want the rate locked before the end of the day.

When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 6918. If they ask for something more, your date of birth is February 11, 1985 and your mailing ZIP code is 78727. You answer only what you are asked.

If the agent asks whether anything changed on the house since you signed, you mention that on October 1 you switched to Elevation A of The Briarwood because it was a better fit, and that the change came with a fee on your purchase statement. If the agent asks about your homesite, it is the cul-de-sac lot you reserved in September. If they ask how you plan to live in the home, it will be your primary residence.

If the agent explains that the loan amount on your lock has to come down and tells you the new amount, you take a breath, say you have savings set aside and can bring the difference at closing, and agree to the change. If the agent tells you there is an amount you need to pay yourself and hands that payment to you, you pay it right away from your checking account by ACH, using exactly the amount the agent gives you, and then read the agent the receipt number you get back. Whenever the agent quotes a figure, you ask once how it was worked out and then accept the explanation.

Once the agent tells you your rate is locked and tells you the rate and the date it runs through, you write both down, thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.lock_expiration_date: Value 2027-07-02. Basis: rule of lock_ext_lock_confirmation: 'The lock date is the confirmation date and the lock expiration date is the lock date plus lock_term_days; where expiry_rolls_to_business_day is true and that day is a Saturday, Sunday or Calloway holiday, the lock runs through the next business day.' 2026-10-05 + 270 days = 2027-07-02, a Friday, so no roll. Uniqueness: single anchor and duration.

edges.condition: lock_events carries lock_fee_paid rows on the lock whose amounts add up to the upfront lock fee due on the lock's current loan amount.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Chain loan resize -> upfront fee -> confirmation: each problem has one prerequisite, so the only topological order is the gold order; the confirmation also reads the resized loan amount, which the chain already places first.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the fee payment leaves no lock_fee_paid row: the locked rate recomputes to 6.599 instead of 6.537 (no buyer-paid fee adjustment) and lock_fee_held stays 0.00 instead of 2,481.89.

Skipping the terms change leaves the loan at 480,141.00: the upfront fee recomputes to 2,901.59 instead of 2,481.89 (floored fee 5,401.59, Calloway's part 2,500.00 / 5,401.59 = 0.4628, below the cap); terminal loan_amount 480,141.00 and ltv_pct 90.00 instead of 442,835.00 and 85.41.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only that the requested 270-day build lock be locked today; it never mentions a fee, a payment being due, the loan amount, loan-to-value or any change to the lock. The plan change is mentioned only if the agent asks whether anything changed, and the payment and loan change appear only as passive reactions after the agent explains them. No prerequisite policy id appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_rate_lock_90ad719f writes status locked, lock date, rate and expiration without reading the ledger; pay_upfront_lock_fee_77612280 posts any amount without checking the loan amount; resize_lock_loan_amount_60b17697 writes the values given. None refuses or hints (task_tools.py bodies).
